concepts.title: Shared Responsibility Model
concepts.summary: Defines what security tasks are handled by the cloud provider (Microsoft) vs. what tasks are retained by the customer across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.
deepDive: In on-premises: Customer manages 100% of the stack (physical datacenter, hypervisor, OS, network, apps, data).

In IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): Cloud provider handles physical security, power, and hardware virtualization. Customer configures and patches OS, network controls, runtime, applications, and protects data.
In PaaS (Platform as a Service): Cloud provider also manages OS patching, hardware, network infrastructure, and database runtime engine. Customer is responsible only for their applications and data.
In SaaS (Software as a Service): Cloud provider manages everything except customer data, identities/credentials, and access rights management.
Exam Rule: The customer ALWAYS retains responsibility for their data, identity governance, accounts, and endpoint devices, regardless of cloud model.
concepts.examTip: Whenever an exam question mentions patching the guest OS, that is ALWAYS the customer's duty in IaaS, but Microsoft's duty in PaaS/SaaS.
concepts.analogy: Like renting a house: In on-premises you build and own the house; in IaaS you rent an unfurnished apartment (landlord fixes the roof, you furnish and lock your doors); in SaaS you book a fully serviced hotel suite.

concepts.title: CapEx vs. OpEx Financial Models
concepts.summary: Capital Expenditure involves upfront spending on physical hardware and facilities, while Operational Expenditure involves ongoing operational costs with pay-as-you-go flexibility.
deepDive: CapEx: Requires substantial upfront capital investments in physical servers, storage arrays, cooling, and real estate.
CapEx value depreciates over accounting life (typically 3-5 years) with fixed capacity limits.
OpEx: Pay-as-you-go pricing model where costs scale directly with actual resource consumption.
OpEx offers agility: businesses can spin up 100 VMs for 3 hours to process analytics and shut them down immediately without idle hardware costs.
concepts.examTip: Azure operates primarily on an OpEx model. Look for keywords like 'no upfront cost', 'pay for what you use', and 'immediate tax deduction as operational cost'.
concepts.analogy: CapEx is like purchasing a commercial lorry with loans and maintenance costs; OpEx is hiring a courier van or ride-share only for the exact delivery trip.

concepts.title: Cloud Deployment Models: Public, Private, Hybrid & Multi-Cloud
concepts.summary: The four deployment architectures defining where infrastructure resides, who owns it, and how resources are shared or isolated.
deepDive: Public Cloud: Owned and operated by a third-party cloud provider (Microsoft Azure). Resources are delivered over the public internet to multiple tenants with zero hardware maintenance.

Private Cloud: Computing infrastructure used exclusively by a single business or organization. Can be hosted in an on-premises datacenter or dedicated off-site facility. Customer has total control but full CapEx costs.
Hybrid Cloud: Combines public cloud with private cloud or on-premises infrastructure, allowing data and apps to be shared between them (e.g., Azure Arc, Azure Stack).
Multi-Cloud: Using multiple public cloud providers simultaneously (e.g., Azure and AWS) to avoid vendor lock-in or meet specific compliance needs.
concepts.examTip: Hybrid Cloud is the only answer when an organization wants to keep sensitive legacy databases on-premises due to legal compliance while running web applications in Azure.
concepts.analogy: Public cloud is public transit (bus/train); Private cloud is owning a personal car; Hybrid cloud is keeping a personal bicycle for village errands and taking the high-speed train for intercity travel.

concepts.title: Cloud Benefits: High Availability, Scalability, Elasticity & Agility
concepts.summary: The fundamental architectural advantages that cloud computing provides over traditional on-premises datacenters.
deepDive: High Availability (HA): Ensuring systems remain operational and accessible with minimal downtime, supported by Microsoft Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
Scalability: The ability of a system to handle increased workload. Vertical scaling (scale up) adds CPU/RAM to a VM; Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds more VM instances.
Elasticity: The ability to automatically add resources during demand surges and automatically deallocate them when traffic drops (Autoscaling), saving costs.
Agility: The speed at which IT teams can provision new environments, test new features, and deploy services globally in minutes rather than months.
Fault Tolerance: The ability of a system to continue operating without interruption even when individual hardware components fail.
concepts.examTip: Scalability is about capacity ceiling; Elasticity is about dynamic automatic scaling up AND down in response to real-time spikes.
concepts.analogy: Elasticity is like an elastic waistband that expands during a heavy feast and contracts back to normal size right after digestion.

concepts.title: Azure Regions, Geographies & Availability Zones
concepts.summary: The global physical footprint of Azure data infrastructure structured into Geographies, Regions, Region Pairs, and Availability Zones.
deepDive: Geography: A discrete market (typically containing two or more regions) that preserves data residency and compliance boundaries (e.g., South Africa).
Region: A geographical area containing one or more datacenters networked through a low-latency, dedicated fiber network (e.g., South Africa North in Johannesburg).
Availability Zones (AZs): Physically separate datacenters within an Azure region. Each zone has its own independent power, cooling, and networking.
A region with AZ support contains at least 3 distinct availability zones.

Region Pairs: Each Azure region is paired with another region in the same geography at least 300 miles apart to protect against regional disasters. Planned updates roll out to paired regions sequentially.
concepts.examTip: Availability Zones protect against datacenter-level failures. Region Pairs protect against large-scale regional catastrophic events (e.g., widespread natural disasters).
concepts.analogy: Availability Zones are three separate bank branches across Nairobi with separate generators; Region Pairs are having duplicate vaults in Nairobi and Mombasa.

concepts.title: Azure Resource Hierarchy: Management Groups, Subscriptions & Resource Groups
concepts.summary: The 4-level organizational hierarchy in Azure: Management Groups > Subscriptions > Resource Groups > Resources.
deepDive: Level 1 - Management Groups: Containers for managing access, policies, and compliance across multiple subscriptions. Can be nested up to 6 levels deep.

Level 2 - Subscriptions: Logical units of Azure services linked to an Azure account. Acts as both an administrative boundary (access control) and a billing boundary (invoices generated per subscription).
Level 3 - Resource Groups: Logical containers where related Azure resources (VMs, storage, virtual networks) are deployed, monitored, and managed as a single unit.
A resource can exist in only ONE resource group at a time. If a resource group is deleted, ALL resources inside it are deleted.
Level 4 - Resources: Individual instances of services like Virtual Machines, Storage Accounts, or SQL Databases.
concepts.examTip: Subscriptions are both a billing boundary and an access boundary. Resource groups do NOT nest inside other resource groups.
concepts.analogy: Think of a school: Management Group is the District Ministry, Subscription is the School Campus account, Resource Group is a classroom, and Resources are the desks and computers inside that classroom.

concepts.title: Azure Compute: Virtual Machines, Scale Sets, App Services & Functions
concepts.summary: Core on-demand computing services ranging from unmanaged IaaS virtual machines to fully managed PaaS web apps and event-driven serverless functions.
deepDive: Azure Virtual Machines (VMs): IaaS service providing total control over operating system, software stack, and configurations. Customer manages OS patching.
Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS): Automatically deploys and balances an identical set of load-balanced VMs based on demand.
Azure App Service: PaaS offering for building, hosting, and scaling web apps and REST APIs in .NET, Java, Node.js, Python, or PHP without managing underlying servers.
Azure Functions: Serverless event-driven compute service that executes code in response to triggers (HTTP requests, database changes, timers) and charges strictly per millisecond of execution.
Azure Container Instances (ACI): Fastest way to run isolated Docker containers in Azure without managing any VM infrastructure.
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Enterprise-grade managed container orchestration platform for deploying and scaling microservices clusters.
concepts.examTip: When a question says 'serverless' and 'event-driven' with 'no charge when idle', the answer is Azure Functions. When it asks for 'PaaS web hosting without managing VMs', it is Azure App Service.
concepts.analogy: Virtual Machines are like hiring a full-time mechanic (IaaS); Azure Functions is like dialing an on-demand taxi ride only when you need to go somewhere (Serverless).

concepts.title: Azure Virtual Network (VNet), Subnets & Network Security Groups (NSGs)
concepts.summary: The fundamental building block for private networking in Azure, enabling secure communication between Azure resources, the internet, and on-premises networks.
deepDive: Azure VNet: A representation of your own network in the cloud, isolated from other tenants.
Subnets: Allow you to segment the VNet into one or more sub-networks for security and organization (e.g., WebSubnet, DatabaseSubnet).
Network Security Groups (NSGs): Virtual firewalls that filter network traffic to and from Azure resources using 5-tuple security rules (Source, Source Port, Destination, Destination Port, Protocol).
Azure Bastion: Fully managed PaaS service that provides secure, seamless RDP/SSH access to VMs directly through the Azure portal via TLS, without exposing public IP addresses on the VMs.
Azure VPN Gateway: Encrypted connection over the public internet connecting an on-premises network to an Azure VNet.
Azure ExpressRoute: Dedicated, private, high-speed fiber connection from on-premises to Microsoft cloud that DOES NOT traverse the public internet.
concepts.examTip: ExpressRoute provides highest speed and security because it bypasses the public internet completely. Azure Bastion eliminates the need for public IPs on VMs for RDP/SSH.
concepts.analogy: A VNet is a gated university campus; Subnets are individual faculty buildings; NSGs are security guards at each building entrance checking student IDs; ExpressRoute is a dedicated private underground tunnel directly from headquarters.

concepts.title: Azure Storage Services: Blob, Files, Disks & Access Tiers
concepts.summary: Massively scalable cloud storage for unstructured data, file shares, and VM disks, paired with cost-optimized lifecycle access tiers.
deepDive: Azure Blob Storage: Object storage optimized for massive amounts of unstructured data (images, videos, backups, logs).
Azure Files: Fully managed SMB/NFS cloud file shares that can be mounted simultaneously by cloud or on-premises Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.
Azure Disk Storage: Block-level storage volumes attached to Azure Virtual Machines (OS disks and Data disks).

Storage Access Tiers: Hot (frequently accessed data, highest storage cost, lowest access cost); Cool (infrequently accessed, stored for at least 30 days); Cold (rarely accessed, stored for at least 90 days); Archive (rarely accessed, lowest storage cost, highest retrieval latency up to several hours).

Redundancy Options: LRS (Locally Redundant - 3 copies in 1 datacenter), ZRS (Zone-Redundant - 3 copies across 3 availability zones in the same region), GRS (Geo-Redundant - 3 copies in primary region + 3 copies in paired region).
concepts.examTip: Archive tier is the cheapest for long-term backups, but files are offline and require hours to rehydrate before you can read them.
concepts.analogy: Hot tier is your kitchen counter (grab snacks immediately); Cool tier is your pantry cupboard; Archive tier is an off-site warehouse where you must request items in advance.

concepts.title: Azure Databases: Azure SQL, Cosmos DB & Database for MySQL/PostgreSQL
concepts.summary: Fully managed relational and NoSQL database services with automatic patching, backups, high availability, and global distribution.
deepDive: Azure SQL Database: Fully managed relational Database-as-a-Service (PaaS) based on the latest stable Microsoft SQL Server engine with built-in high availability and AI performance tuning.
Azure Cosmos DB: Globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database service offering single-digit millisecond response times at any scale with 99.999% SLA.
Supports APIs for MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table, and SQL (Core).
Azure Database for MySQL & PostgreSQL: Fully managed open-source relational databases in Azure.
Azure Synapse Analytics: Enterprise analytics service that accelerates time to insight across data warehouses and big data systems.
concepts.examTip: If an exam question requires single-digit millisecond latency and turnkey global replication for NoSQL data, the answer is ALWAYS Azure Cosmos DB.
concepts.analogy: Azure SQL is an organized structured library catalog; Cosmos DB is an ultra-fast global courier dispatch network that can handle any package shape instantly in 50 countries.

concepts.title: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) & Identity Management
concepts.summary: Cloud-based identity and access management service providing single sign-on, authentication, and authorization for cloud and hybrid applications.
deepDive: Entra ID vs. Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS): Entra ID is a multi-tenant cloud identity service using REST APIs and modern protocols (SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect), whereas traditional AD DS uses LDAP and Kerberos.
Single Sign-On (SSO): Users log in once and gain access to Microsoft 365, Azure Portal, and thousands of SaaS applications.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Requires two or more verification factors: something you know (password), something you have (phone/authenticator app), or something you are (biometrics/fingerprint).
Conditional Access: If-then policy engine (e.g., If user is signing in from outside country OR from an unmanaged device, Then require MFA or block access).
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Grants fine-grained permissions to security principals (users, groups, service principals) on Azure resources based on roles (Owner, Contributor, Reader).
concepts.examTip: Authentication confirms WHO you are (identity verification); Authorization determines WHAT you have permission to do (RBAC permissions).
concepts.analogy: Authentication is showing your national ID passport at airport immigration; Authorization is your boarding pass ticket that decides whether you sit in First Class or Economy.

concepts.title: Azure Governance: Azure Policy, Resource Locks & Tags
concepts.summary: Tools to enforce corporate organizational standards, prevent accidental resource deletion, and track cloud expenditures across departments.
deepDive: Azure Policy: Evaluates resources and enforces rules to ensure compliance with corporate standards and service level agreements (e.g., Allow only VMs of size D-series, Restrict deployment to South Africa North region, Enforce tags).
Initiatives (Policy Sets): Collections of multiple policy definitions grouped together to achieve a single overarching compliance goal (e.g., ISO 27001 or PCI-DSS).
Resource Locks: Prevent accidental deletion or modification of critical Azure resources.
CanNotDelete Lock: Authorized users can read and modify a resource, but CANNOT delete it.
ReadOnly Lock: Authorized users can read a resource, but CANNOT delete or modify it.
Resource Tags: Key-value metadata pairs added to resources to organize billing, cost allocation, environment management, and ownership tracking.
concepts.examTip: Resource locks take precedence over RBAC permissions! Even a Subscription Owner cannot delete a resource that has a CanNotDelete lock until the lock is removed.
concepts.analogy: Azure Policy is the municipal building code (inspectors reject unapproved floor plans); Resource Locks are the child-safety lock on car windows that prevents passengers from falling out.

concepts.title: Cost Management: Azure Budgets, Pricing Calculator & TCO
concepts.summary: Tools to estimate costs, analyze cloud expenditure, configure automated budget alerts, and compare on-premises datacenter costs against Azure.
deepDive: Pricing Calculator: Pre-deployment tool used to estimate anticipated monthly costs for new Azure solutions based on configuration and usage assumptions.
Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator: Tool used to compare the comprehensive cost of running existing on-premises datacenter workloads against running them in Azure over a 5-year period.
TCO factors in server hardware, electricity, cooling, datacenter real estate, network bandwidth, storage arrays, and IT labor overhead.
Microsoft Cost Management: Post-deployment service to monitor historical spending, analyze trends, and set spending limits.
Azure Budgets: Configurable financial thresholds that trigger automated email notifications or action groups when spending reaches 80% or 100% of budgeted amounts.
concepts.examTip: Use TCO Calculator to justify migrating existing on-premises servers to Azure before the migration; use Pricing Calculator to estimate the specific bill for cloud resources.
concepts.analogy: Pricing Calculator is reading the grocery store menu before dining; TCO Calculator is calculating how much cheaper eating at home vs. running a private kitchen for 5 years would be.

concepts.title: Azure Monitoring: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics & Azure Advisor
concepts.summary: Full-stack observability tools to collect telemetries, analyze logs, generate real-time alerts, and obtain actionable best-practice recommendations.
deepDive: Azure Monitor: Comprehensive solution for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry from cloud and on-premises environments (Metrics and Logs).
Log Analytics: Tool in the Azure portal used to query and analyze log data using Kusto Query Language (KQL).
Application Insights: Feature of Azure Monitor that monitors live web applications, detecting performance anomalies and diagnosing bottlenecks.
Azure Service Health: Personalized dashboard keeping you informed about the health of Azure services and regions you use, planned maintenance, and incident root cause analyses.
Azure Advisor: Personalized cloud consultant analyzing your resource configurations to provide recommendations across 5 pillars: Cost, Security, Reliability, Performance, and Operational Excellence.
concepts.examTip: Azure Service Health tells you when MICROSOFT has an outage affecting your services; Azure Monitor tells you how YOUR own apps and resources are performing.
concepts.analogy: Azure Monitor is your vehicle dashboard showing engine RPM, speed, and fuel; Azure Advisor is a certified master mechanic sitting beside you giving tips on how to save fuel and drive safer.

questions.question: An organization wants to migrate its on-premises infrastructure to Azure. Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which responsibility is ALWAYS retained by the customer regardless of whether they choose IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS?
options: Data classification, accounts, and identity management
Hardware virtualization and host server maintenance
questions.explanation: In all cloud deployment types (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and on-premises), the customer ALWAYS maintains ownership and accountability for their data, endpoint devices, accounts, and identity governance.
whyWrong: OS patching is managed by the cloud provider in PaaS and SaaS solutions.
Physical datacenter infrastructure and security are always managed entirely by Microsoft in the cloud.
Correct answer.
Hardware virtualization is handled by Microsoft's hypervisors in all cloud services.

questions.question: A startup plans to launch a seasonal marketing campaign where web traffic might surge by 1,000% for one weekend and drop back to normal on Monday. Which cloud characteristic enables resources to automatically scale out during the spike and deallocate when traffic subsides?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the dynamic ability of a cloud system to automatically provision additional computing resources during demand surges and automatically deallocate them when load decreases, preventing overpayment for idle capacity.
whyWrong: Fault tolerance ensures zero disruption during hardware component failure, but does not add or remove capacity dynamically.
Correct answer.
Predictable latency refers to consistent network response times, not automated scaling.
High availability keeps systems operational with high uptime, but does not describe the automated expansion/contraction of resources.

questions.question: A multinational financial enterprise requires a solution that guarantees their applications can withstand an entire datacenter outage within an Azure region without suffering downtime. What should they deploy?
options: Multiple resources across Availability Zones in the region
A single Virtual Machine with Locally Redundant Storage (LRS)
Two separate Resource Groups within the same datacenter
An Azure Policy restricting deployment to a single region
questions.explanation: Availability Zones are physically distinct datacenters within an Azure region, each equipped with independent power, cooling, and network connections. Deploying across Availability Zones protects against datacenter-level failures.
whyWrong: Correct answer.
A single VM with LRS replicates data 3 times within a single datacenter, so a datacenter power outage will take it offline.
Resource Groups are logical management boundaries and do not provide physical isolation or fault tolerance.
Azure Policy enforces compliance rules and does not provide high-availability architecture.

questions.question: Which Azure compute service allows developers to execute event-driven code in response to HTTP requests or message queues without managing servers, and charges strictly for the milliseconds the code runs?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is Microsoft's flagship serverless compute solution. It executes code upon external triggers and charges only when code is executing, with zero cost when idle.
whyWrong: Virtual Machine Scale Sets require managing and paying for underlying VM instances even when idle.
Correct answer.
Azure Container Instances runs containerized workloads, but is not primarily a serverless function platform billed by milliseconds.
Azure App Service Dedicated tier incurs continuous monthly hourly pricing regardless of traffic.

questions.question: An administrator needs to ensure that even users assigned the 'Owner' role on a critical production Azure subscription CANNOT accidentally delete the production SQL Database or its virtual network. What should the administrator apply?
options: A CanNotDelete Resource Lock on the resource group
An Azure Policy with an 'AuditIfNotExists' effect
A Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policy
questions.explanation: Resource Locks override RBAC permissions. A CanNotDelete lock permits authorized users (including Subscription Owners) to read and modify resources, but strictly blocks deletion until the lock itself is explicitly removed.
whyWrong: A ReadOnly role would prevent the team from making valid routine configuration updates to the database.
Correct answer.
Azure Policy with AuditIfNotExists only logs compliance warnings and does not block deletion in real-time.
Conditional Access evaluates sign-in conditions (MFA, IP location), not specific Azure resource deletion actions.

questions.question: Which tool should a company use to compare the estimated financial cost of maintaining their on-premises datacenter hardware, power, cooling, and administration over 5 years against migrating those workloads to Azure?
questions.explanation: The TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) Calculator is designed specifically to estimate cost savings realized by migrating existing on-premises server infrastructure, storage, and networking workloads to Microsoft Azure.
whyWrong: Pricing Calculator estimates individual Azure service bills before deployment, but does not model on-premises datacenter hardware or real estate comparisons.
Correct answer.
Azure Budgets sets spending alerts on currently deployed cloud resources.
Azure Advisor provides optimization tips for resources already running in an active Azure subscription.

flashcards.front: What is the Shared Responsibility Model?
flashcards.back: A security framework dividing operational duties between Microsoft and the customer. You always control data, identities, and endpoints; Microsoft controls physical datacenters and host hypervisors.
flashcards.analogy: Renting an apartment: the landlord maintains the structure, but you are responsible for locking your door and safeguarding your personal property.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between CapEx and OpEx?
flashcards.back: CapEx involves large upfront physical investments depreciated over years. OpEx is ongoing pay-as-you-go consumption with no upfront cost and immediate tax deduction.
flashcards.analogy: CapEx is buying a farm truck; OpEx is hiring a delivery boda-boda or courier per trip.

flashcards.front: What is an Azure Availability Zone?
flashcards.back: Physically distinct datacenters within the same Azure region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. A zone-enabled region has at least 3 distinct zones.
flashcards.analogy: Three independent bank branches in Nairobi connected by private fiber; if one suffers a transformer blowout, the other two keep operating uninterrupted.

flashcards.back: A dedicated private fiber connection from your on-premises network to Azure that does NOT travel across the public internet, ensuring maximum speed and security.
flashcards.analogy: A private underground high-speed rail line directly between your corporate headquarters and the central airport.

flashcards.front: What is a CanNotDelete Resource Lock?
flashcards.back: A protective governance lock that allows authorized users to read and modify a resource, but prevents anyone—including Subscription Owners—from deleting it.
flashcards.analogy: A tamper-proof safety seal on an emergency fire valve that prevents accidental shutdown.
